chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who seeks the pleasure of the people by incurring the anger of Allah, Allah will make his praise from the people as a condemnation.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to a person who seeks people's pleasure by angering God?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on obedience to creatures versus the Creator, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the Shia concept of *ikhlas* (sincerity) by warning that compromising divine command for social approval leads to a paradoxical reversal of reputation. Scholarly commentary notes that this 'condemnation' often manifests as the loss of inner peace and the erosion of credibility, as the individual becomes a slave to public opinion rather than a servant of God. This principle is central to understanding the balance between social conduct (*mu'amalat*) and spiritual integrity (*ibadat*) in Shia ethics.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who seeks the pleasure of the people by Angering Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Make his praise from the people as a condemnation’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Whoever seeks the pleasure of people to anger Allah, Allah will make the people who praise him vilify.’”
